stem: A drone's position, in meters, at time t seconds (0 ≤ t ≤ 12) is r(t) = ⟨t² − 6t, 12t − t²⟩, with x measured east and y measured north. For which times is the drone moving east and north at the same time?

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: A ball rolling across a table has position, in centimeters, r(t) = ⟨t² − 10t, 16t − t²⟩ for 0 ≤ t ≤ 16, with x to the right and y up. For which times is the ball moving right and up at the same time?

subject: AP Precalculus

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: A bakery chain's weekly sales matrix S has rows for 2 stores and columns for 3 products, so S = [10 20 5; 8 0 12] counts items sold. The price matrix P = [3; 2; 4] lists the price in dollars of each product. Which statement about computing the weekly revenue of each store is correct?

choices.t: PS is defined and gives the same totals, because matrix products can be taken in either order.
SP is defined, is 3×1, and gives one total for each of the 3 columns of S.
SP is undefined, because S has 2 rows while P has 3 rows.
SP is defined, is 2×1, and equals [90; 72], with one entry for each of the 2 rows of S.

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: A café tracks hours worked with a matrix S whose rows are 3 employees and whose columns are 2 shifts, so S = [4 6; 5 2; 0 9]. The pay matrix P = [7; 3] gives the hourly wage in dollars for each shift. Which statement about computing each employee's total pay is correct?

choices.t: PS is defined and gives the same totals, because matrix products can be taken in either order.
SP is defined, is 2×1, and gives one total for each of the 2 columns of S.
SP is defined, is 3×1, and equals [46; 41; 27], with one entry for each of the 3 rows of S.
SP is undefined, because S has 3 rows while P has 2 rows.

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: A warehouse records shipments in a matrix S with rows for 2 trucks and columns for 4 goods, so S = [2 1 0 3; 4 5 1 0] counts crates. The weight matrix P = [5; 8; 2; 1] gives the weight in kilograms of one crate of each good. Which statement about computing the total weight carried by each truck is correct?

choices.t: SP is defined, is 2×1, and equals [21; 62], with one entry for each of the 2 rows of S.
PS is defined and gives the same totals, because matrix products can be taken in either order.
SP is defined, is 4×1, and gives one total for each of the 4 columns of S.
SP is undefined, because S has 2 rows while P has 4 rows.

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: A theater's ticket matrix S has rows for 3 shows and columns for 2 ticket types, so S = [6 1; 2 3; 4 4] counts tickets sold. The price matrix P = [10; 5] lists the price in dollars of each ticket type. Which statement about computing the revenue from each show is correct?

choices.t: PS is defined and gives the same totals, because matrix products can be taken in either order.
SP is defined, is 3×1, and equals [65; 35; 60], with one entry for each of the 3 rows of S.
SP is defined, is 2×1, and gives one total for each of the 2 columns of S.
SP is undefined, because S has 3 rows while P has 2 rows.

subject: AP Precalculus

subject: AP Precalculus

The image has area 30 square units, and its orientation is reversed.
The image has area 42 square units, and its orientation is reversed.
The image has area -30 square units, and its orientation is reversed.

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: A streaming service has two plans, X and Y. Each week 80% of X subscribers stay on X and 20% move to Y; 30% of Y subscribers move to X and 70% stay on Y. The state vector is [X; Y], and M = [0.8 0.3; 0.2 0.7] updates it from one week to the next (each column describes where that plan's subscribers go). Now there are 500 subscribers on X and 300 on Y. How many are predicted on [X; Y] after two weeks?

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: People in a metro area live in the city (C) or the suburbs (S). Each year 90% of city residents stay and 10% move to the suburbs; 20% of suburban residents move to the city and 80% stay. With state vector [C; S], the yearly update matrix is M = [0.9 0.2; 0.1 0.8] (each column describes where that group's residents go). The population is now 600 thousand in the city and 400 thousand in the suburbs. What is predicted for [C; S] after two years?

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: A bike-share network has stations in the north (N) and south (S). Each day 60% of bikes at N stay there and 40% end the day at S; 50% of bikes at S end at N and 50% stay. With state vector [N; S], the daily update matrix is M = [0.6 0.5; 0.4 0.5] (each column describes where bikes from that station end up). Today there are 200 bikes at N and 100 at S. How many are predicted at [N; S] after two days?

subject: AP Precalculus
stem: A town's voters prefer party P or party Q. Each election 70% of P voters stay with P and 30% switch to Q; 40% of Q voters switch to P and 60% stay. With state vector [P; Q], the update matrix is M = [0.7 0.4; 0.3 0.6] (each column describes where that party's voters go). Currently 800 voters prefer P and 200 prefer Q. What is predicted for [P; Q] after two elections?
